questions.question_text: In a survey of $100$ students, $31$ chose the library as their favourite place. What percentage chose the library?

options.why: Subtracted $31$ from $100$ and reported the percentage who did not choose the library.
Divided $31$ by $10$, shifting the value one place too far for a group of $100$.
Multiplied $31$ by $10$, making the part larger than the whole instead of writing it per hundred.
Used the complement to $100$ and described the part not included.
Read the number as a count of wholes instead of a number of parts per hundred.
Used a denominator of $10$ even though percent means per hundred.
Counted the unshaded squares instead of the shaded squares.
Reversed the six full shaded columns and four extra squares when writing the two digits.
Counted only the six complete shaded columns and ignored the four extra shaded squares.

questions.question_text: A tank contains its entire capacity. Which percentage describes the amount in the tank?

options.why: Confused one whole with one part out of one hundred.
Treated a full tank as half of the whole rather than the complete whole.
Used the percentage for none even though the tank is completely full.

questions.question_text: A tray has none of its spaces filled. Which percentage is filled?

options.why: Used the percentage for the whole tray instead of the filled part, which is empty.
Assumed one tenth was filled even though the stem states that no spaces are filled.
Used one part per hundred even though there are no filled parts.

questions.question_text: A whole bar and one-half of a second equal bar are shaded. What percentage of one bar is shaded altogether?

options.why: Counted only the fully shaded bar and ignored the additional half bar.
Counted only the half bar and ignored the complete shaded bar.
Treated one-half as $5\%$ instead of $50\%$ when combining it with the whole.

questions.question_text: A report says $70\%$ of $200$ visitors used the main gate. Which statement is true?

options.text: The report means $70$ out of every $100$ visitors.
Exactly $70$ visitors used the main gate.
options.why: Treated $70\%$ as a fixed count of $70$ rather than a proportion of the $200$ visitors.

options.text: All $200$ visitors used the main gate.
options.why: Treated a percentage below $100\%$ as the whole group.

options.text: No visitors used the main gate.
options.why: Confused a positive percentage with $0\%$, which represents none.
